data.title: BCRLS Inaugural Lecture Series
data.description: BCRLS inaugural lecture series featuring academic discussions on refugee law, displacement and refugee protection.

detail.description: The BCRLS inaugural lecture series featured three distinguished speakers addressing ethnography of refugees, global burden-sharing, and legal challenges of boat refugees, marking the beginning of BCRLS’s academic journey.
detail.programme: A three-speaker inaugural lecture series focused on refugee ethnography, global burden-sharing and the legal challenges faced by boat refugees.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS)

Dr. Hassan Faruk Al Imran — Associate Professor (Law), Independent University Bangladesh
Professor Dr. Rakiba Nabi — Chairman, Department of Law, University of Chittagong

data.description: Academic discussion concerning displacement, statelessness, refugee protection and migration governance.

The discussion covered climate-induced displacement, statelessness, refugee protection gaps, and the intersection of artificial intelligence with migration governance, contributing to regional discourse on refugee law in South Asia.

data.title: Field Visit to Bhasan Char
data.description: A BCRLS field research visit focusing on higher education access and livelihood opportunities for Rohingya refugees.

detail.description: A BCRLS field visit to Bhasan Char conducted as part of the research project “Legal Aspects of Higher Education Access and Livelihood through Income-Generating Activities for the Rohingyas in Bangladesh.” The visit aimed to gather first-hand insights and empirical data on legal and practical challenges surrounding education access and livelihood opportunities for Rohingya refugees.
detail.programme: Field engagement in Bhasan Char focused on education access, livelihood opportunities, empirical research and evidence-based policy analysis.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS)
speakers: BCRLS Directors and Executive Members

data.imageAlt: Seminar on Foundations of Refugee Law
data.title: Seminar on Foundations of Refugee Law
data.description: Academic seminar discussing the foundations, principles and contemporary challenges of refugee law.

detail.description: On 19 January 2026 at Jagannath University, BCRLS in collaboration with the Department of Law and Land Administration, Jagannath University, hosted the academic seminar “Foundations of Refugee Law: Principles, Protection, and Contemporary Challenges.”
detail.programme: Discussion on core principles of refugee law, evolving protection frameworks and contemporary challenges in refugee protection.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS), in collaboration with the Department of Law and Land Administration, Jagannath University
speakers: Sakhawat Sajjat Sejan — Speaker
Honourable Christine Richardson — Chief Guest
Meftahul Hasan — Special Guest, Assistant Professor, Department of Law, Jagannath University

data.imageAlt: Asylum Under International Refugee Law and in South Asia
data.title: Asylum Under International Refugee Law and in South Asia
data.description: A comparative academic discussion on asylum under international refugee law and within the South Asian context.

detail.description: BCRLS, in collaboration with the NSU Center for Legal Research (NSU CLR), presented the special lecture “Asylum Under International Refugee Law and in South Asia: A Comparative Analysis.” The programme was held on 10 April 2026 from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM at the Moot Court Room (NAC 616), North South University.
detail.programme: Comparative examination of asylum law in South Asia within the broader framework of international refugee law and international protection.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS) in collaboration with the NSU Center for Legal Research (NSU CLR)
speakers: Dr. Simon Behrman — Associate Professor, School of Law, University of Warwick

data.imageAlt: Academic Dialogue on the Rohingya Genocide
data.title: Academic Dialogue on the Rohingya Genocide
data.description: An academic dialogue focusing on scholarship, legal recognition and accountability concerning the Rohingya genocide.

detail.description: BCRLS convened a high-level academic dialogue with Professor Kjell Anderson of the University of Manitoba Law School (Canada), centering on evolving scholarship surrounding the Rohingya genocide. The discussion examined legal recognition, evidentiary challenges and international accountability, situating the Rohingya crisis within the wider theme of “Forgotten Genocides” in South Asia.
detail.programme: Scholarly discussion on the Rohingya genocide, legal recognition, evidentiary challenges and international accountability.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS)
speakers: Professor Kjell Anderson — University of Manitoba Law School, Canada

data.imageAlt: Administrative and Judicial Governance of Refugees
data.title: Administrative and Judicial Governance of Refugees
data.description: BCRLS, in collaboration with the Department of Law, Canadian University of Bangladesh, organized a seminar on refugee protection, non-refoulement, arrest, detention and administrative challenges in Bangladesh.

detail.description: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS), in collaboration with the Department of Law, Canadian University of Bangladesh, successfully organized the seminar titled “Administrative and Judicial Governance of Refugees: Protection, Non-Refoulement, Arrest, Detention and Administrative Challenges in Bangladesh.” The session featured meaningful discussion on refugee protection, non-refoulement, detention and administrative challenges within Bangladesh’s legal framework, with participation from more than 50 participants.
detail.programme: A seminar examining refugee protection, non-refoulement, arrest, detention and administrative governance challenges in Bangladesh.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS), in collaboration with the Department of Law, Canadian University of Bangladesh
speakers: Dr. Md. Rizwanul Islam — Professor of Law & Dean (SHSS), North South University
Ahmad Ibrahim — Advisor, Displacement and Climate Justice, BLAST
Mohammad Sunzad Sheikh — Assistant Professor & Head, Department of Law, Canadian University of Bangladesh
Md. Riad Mahmud — Senior Lecturer, East West University; Session Moderator

data.imageAlt: From Norms to Ground Realities: Citizenship, Justice and the Rohingya Integration Dilemma
data.title: From Norms to Ground Realities: Citizenship, Justice and the Rohingya Integration Dilemma
data.description: A BCRLS panel discussion engaging with refugee protection, citizenship, justice and practical pathways surrounding the Rohingya integration dilemma in Bangladesh.

detail.description: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS) successfully organized the panel discussion titled “From Norms to Ground Realities: Citizenship, Justice and the Rohingya Integration Dilemma” at the Centre for Advanced Studies in Humanities, Theatre Hall, University of Dhaka. The session brought together academics, researchers, students and practitioners to critically engage with refugee protection, citizenship, justice and the continuing challenges surrounding the Rohingya crisis in Bangladesh.
detail.programme: The discussion focused on practical and policy-oriented pathways for refugee protection, dignified and regulated income-generating opportunities, regional and international diplomatic engagement, and conditions for safe, voluntary and sustainable repatriation.
detail.organizer: Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS)
speakers: Mr. Md Abu Bakar Siddique — discussion on protection of refugees in non-signatory states
Mr. Nafiz Ahmed — discussion on citizenship law and local integration
Mr. Riad Mahmud — Session Moderator
Ms. Nabila Farhin — Opening Remarks
Mr. Sakhawat Sajjat Sejan — Closing Remarks

data.title: ICERPASA 2026
data.description: International conference on evolving refugee protection architectures in South Asia, bringing together academic and policy perspectives on refugee protection.

detail.description:
The International Conference on Evolving Refugee Protection Architectures in SouthAsia 2026 (ICERPASA 2026) was successfully held on June 27, 2026. Organized by the Department of Law, University of Chittagong, in collaboration with the Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS), this prestigious event served as a vital regional platform for advancing scholarship, policy dialogue, and cooperation on forced migration and human rights.

The conference brought together a distinguished gathering of members from the judiciary, academia, government institutions, international organizations, and humanitarian sectors. Through rigorous academic sessions, thought-provoking discussions, and research presentations, ICERPASA 2026 successfully fostered collaborative approaches and key recommendations to address contemporary refugee and displacement challenges across South Asia.
detail.programme: Regional academic and policy conference on evolving refugee protection architectures in South Asia, featuring academic sessions, research presentations, policy dialogue and discussion on forced migration and human rights.
detail.organizer: Department of Law, University of Chittagong, in collaboration with the Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS)
speakers: Members of the judiciary, academia, government institutions, international organizations, and humanitarian sectors

data.title: Certificate Course on Refugee Law and Statelessness: Foundation to Practice
data.shortDescription: BCRLS inaugural certificate course on refugee law and statelessness, delivered through 20 substantive online lectures with Bangladesh/Rohingya and comparative case studies.
data.description: BCRLS Launches Its Inaugural Certificate Course on Refugee Law and Statelessness: Foundation to Practice. The course is scheduled for October–December 2026 in hybrid format and includes 20 substantive lectures, interactive activities and a 100-mark online final examination.
speakers: International faculty and resource persons — see the course materials
data.programme: 20 substantive topics covering refugee law, statelessness, international protection, displacement, legal frameworks and comparative crises. The Bangladesh/Rohingya situation is used as a primary case study.

data.name: Sakhawat Sajjat Sejan
data.bio: Sakhawat Sajjat Sejan is the Founder of BCRLS. He completed his LL.B. (Hons.) and LL.M. from the University of Chittagong. He is currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Law at University of Information Technology and Sciences. Previously, he worked as an Assistant Professor of Law at the Bangladesh University of Bangladesh and Feni University, where he also served as Head of the Department. He is an active researcher and writer on refugee law and protection.

data.name: Raspiatur Rashpi
data.fullRole: Director, Head of Resource Management, Training & Development
data.bio: Raspiatur Rashpi is currently working as a lecturer, Department of Law, University of Chittagong. She was also the former lecturer in Law, Bangladesh Army International University of Science and Technology. She completed her LLB (Honours) and LLM from Department of Law, University of Chittagong. Her research area of interest includes Climate Change and Environmental laws, Human Rights law, Constitutional law, Refugee law etc.

data.name: Niaz Mohammad
data.bio: Niaz Mohammad is currently working as an Associate Legal Counsel at BRAC and serves as the Director of Research at BCRLS. He previously worked as a Legal Research Assistant at the Centre for Peace and Justice, where he focused on refugee law, including access to justice for Rohingyas in Bangladesh. He completed his LL.B. with distinction from BRAC University and holds a Diploma in Economic, Social and Development Rights from Kathmandu School of Law.

data.name: Md. Rahul Hasan Joy
data.bio: Md. Rahul Hasan Joy completed his BA.LL.B. (Hons.) from Aligarh Muslim University, India, and his LL.M. in International Law from the University of Rajshahi. He is currently a Lecturer in the Department of Law at the University of Information Technology and Sciences (UITS). Previously, he served as a Lecturer of Law at Feni University. He is also an enrolled Advocate with the Bangladesh Bar Council.

data.name: Mohammad Tawhidul Islam Hridoy
data.bio: Mohammad Tawhidul Islam is a Lecturer in the Department of Law at the State University of Bangladesh and currently serves as Director of IT at BCRLS. He previously taught at Feni University and worked at US-Bangla Airlines in Company Secretary and Legal Affairs. He completed his LL.B. and LL.M. from Jahangirnagar University and obtained another LL.M. from South Asian University, New Delhi. His interests include teaching, research, and academic engagement activities.

data.name: Nabila Farhin
data.bio: Nabila Farhin completed her LL.B. (Hons.) and LL.M. (Thesis) from the University of Chittagong, where she ranked among the top students of her class. She also earned an MSS in Industrial Relations and Labour Studies from the University of Dhaka and a Diploma in Economic, Social and Development Rights from Kathmandu School of Law, Nepal. She is currently a Senior Lecturer at East West University and an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. Previously, she served as Staff Captain in the Judge Advocate General’s Office of the Bangladesh Army and worked as a consultant with TIB, ILO, and BLAST. Her research focuses on labour rights, gender justice, and climate justice.

data.name: Md. Riad Mahmud
data.bio: Md. Riad Mahmud is currently serving as a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Law at East West University. He is also an Erasmus Mundus Scholar and serves as an Advisor to Jessup Bangladesh. With experience in legal education, research, and international academic collaboration, he brings strong leadership to BCRLS. As Director of Administration and Finance, he contributes to strengthening the organization’s administrative structure, financial governance, and institutional development.

data.name: Sumaiya Islam
data.bio: Sumaiya Islam completed her LL.B. (Hons.) and LL.M. from Southern University Bangladesh and an additional LL.M. from South Asian University. She is currently a Lecturer in the Department of Law at Manarat International University. She contributes to public engagement, awareness-building, and institutional networking at BCRLS.

data.name: Md. Omar Farque
data.bio: Md. Omar Farque completed both his LL.B. (Hons.) and LL.M. from Eastern University, where he achieved outstanding academic results, including a Gold Medal in his LL.M. He is currently a Lecturer in Law at Eastern University. Previously, he served as a Lecturer in Law at the European University of Bangladesh. He also works as a Senior Research Associate at I. H. Khan & Associates and as an Assistant Editor at Revival Press. His research interests include Public International Law, Refugee Law, Climate Law, and Islamic Law.

Advancing refugee law through knowledge, research & justice.

Call for Blog Writing
Non-Refoulement
Call for original and thoughtful blog contributions on refugee law, forced displacement, statelessness, human rights, and contemporary humanitarian challenges.
Please submit your blog in Microsoft Word (.docx) format, along with a short author biography of 50–80 words.
BCRLS welcomes research, reflection, and reform-oriented writing that contributes to more humane and effective refugee protection frameworks.

The Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS) invites original blog submissions for its academic blog Non-Refoulement from students, academics, researchers, legal professionals, and scholars who are interested in refugee law, forced displacement, statelessness, and contemporary humanitarian challenges.

Refugee law is evolving rapidly in response to changing global realities. Armed conflicts, climate-induced displacement, border governance, statelessness, and gaps in international and domestic legal frameworks continue to raise complex legal and policy questions.
Through this blog initiative, BCRLS seeks to create a platform for informed, critical, and solution-oriented discussions that contribute to the development of refugee law and policy.

We particularly encourage submissions that move beyond description and engage with limitations, inconsistencies, and implementation challenges of existing refugee law frameworks while proposing practical legal, institutional, and policy reforms capable of addressing contemporary displacement challenges.

The Bangladesh Journal of Refugee Law and Displacement Studies (BJRLDs) provides a scholarly platform for critical, interdisciplinary, and globally relevant research on refugee law, forced displacement, statelessness, human rights, and migration.

The Bangladesh Journal of Refugee Law and Displacement Studies (BJRLDs) is dedicated to advancing critical scholarship and interdisciplinary research concerning refugee law, forced displacement, statelessness, human rights, and migration.
The Journal seeks to encourage academic dialogue among scholars, researchers, practitioners, policymakers, and students working on contemporary issues of displacement and protection.
The Journal brings together distinguished scholars and academics from Bangladesh, Australia, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States.
Authors are encouraged to prepare their manuscripts carefully and ensure that submissions meet the Journal's academic and ethical standards.
BJRLDs is committed to maintaining high standards of academic integrity, originality, transparency, and responsible scholarly communication.

Authors, reviewers, editors, and other contributors are expected to uphold ethical standards throughout the publication process and to ensure that scholarly work is presented accurately and responsibly.
The current issue of BJRLDs provides a platform for critical scholarship on refugee law, forced displacement, statelessness, human rights, and migration.

Welcome to the Bangladesh Center for Refugee Law Studies (BCRLS).
BCRLS is committed to advancing research, education and informed dialogue on refugee law, forced displacement, migration and human rights.

Through research, publications, education, seminars, discussions and collaboration, BCRLS seeks to create meaningful opportunities for students, researchers, academics, legal professionals and other stakeholders to engage with important questions surrounding displacement and protection.
We believe that sustained academic engagement and knowledge-sharing can contribute to better understanding, stronger institutions and more rights-based approaches to refugee protection.
We invite students, researchers, practitioners, institutions and interested individuals to engage with BCRLS and contribute to this important conversation.
